objective.statement: Count the lines and spaces of a stave from the bottom, and say where a note sits.
successCriteria: I know a stave has five lines and four spaces.
I always count from the bottom.
I can say whether a note is on a line or in a space, and which one.

explanation.text: Music is written on a stave. A stave has five lines, with four spaces in between.

music.textAlternative: A stave with five notes, one on each line, labelled 1st to 5th from the bottom.

explanation.caption: Five lines. The bottom line is the 1st line, and we count upwards.

music.textAlternative: A stave with four notes, one in each space, labelled 1st to 4th from the bottom.

explanation.caption: Four spaces, also counted from the bottom. The gap above the bottom line is the 1st space.

explanation.text: A note is either on a line, with the line running through the middle of its head, or in a space, sitting between two lines.
The higher a note sits on the stave, the higher it sounds. The curly sign at the start is a clef; it tells us the name of each note, and that comes in the next lessons.
If you lose your place, point at the bottom line and count up: 1st line, 1st space, 2nd line, 2nd space, and so on.

music.textAlternative: Nine notes climbing the stave one step at a time: line, space, line, space and so on, from the bottom line up to the top line.

steps: Tap the bottom note, then the next one up, and keep going. You are touching line, space, line, space ...
Listen: every step up the stave sounds higher.
Say each place out loud as you tap: 1st line, 1st space, 2nd line, 2nd space ...
Which notes are on lines? Which are in spaces? Notice they alternate.
demonstration.textAlternative: Nine notes climbing a treble stave, alternating line and space from the bottom line to the top line. Each can be tapped to hear that it sounds higher than the one before.

4.reason: You have counted the lines when the question is about spaces (or the other way round). There is always one more line than there are spaces.

hints: Count from the bottom: the bottom line is the 1st line.

feedback.correct: Five lines. And there is always one fewer space than lines.

mistakes.line-space-swap: Look closely: is the line running through the note-head, or is the note sitting between two lines?
mistakes.clef-confusion: That would be right in another clef. Check the clef at the start of the stave first.
mistakes.counted-from-top: Lines and spaces are counted from the bottom of the stave upwards.
mistakes.off-by-step: You're one step away. Find a note you know for certain and count up or down from it.
mistakes.ledger-miscount: Count the ledger lines one at a time, from the stave outwards.
mistakes.accidental-ignored: The letter is right, but check for a sharp, flat or natural — in the key signature or in front of the note.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Start from the clef and count from a note you know.
